notes: Read all 90 source lines line by line before editing. The hook composes a localStorage+Context selected-vehicle store with a four-tier precedence: URL path param (web L48-51), URL query param (web L53-55), persisted store (web L44), then first-vehicle default (web L69). On React Native the two URL tiers are browser-router-only (react-router-dom) and the store's localStorage backing is browser-only, so the port collapses to the native-safe store > first-vehicle precedence already established by VehicleSelect.tsx, useHiddenSeries.ts and useNotificationListener.ts. Behavior, state names, the SelectedVehicleResult shape and the parseId/default/memo logic are otherwise preserved verbatim.

L1 `import { useEffect, useMemo } from 'react'` -> `import {useEffect, useMemo, useSyncExternalStore} from 'react'`: useEffect (default-to-first-vehicle effect) and useMemo (vehicle lookup) are preserved; useSyncExternalStore is added to read the inlined module-level store (the native analogue of the web Context). L2 `import { useMatch, useSearchParams } from 'react-router-dom'` REMOVED — the parity tree pulls in no RN router, so the path/query precedence tiers are structurally unavailable (same drop as useHiddenSeries.ts useUrlArray and VehicleSelect.tsx). L3 `import { useVehicles } from '@/api/hooks/useVehicles'` -> `import {useVehicles, type Vehicle} from '../api/hooks/useVehicles'`. L4 `import { useSelectedVehicleStore } from '@/store/selectedVehicle'` REMOVED — replaced by an inlined module-level external store (RN has no localStorage / Context provider wiring in the parity tree). L5 `import type { Vehicle } from '@/types/vehicle'` folded into the L3 import: the ported useVehicles `Vehicle` export is the identical superset shape (snake_case + camelCase aliases + extended detail fields) AND is exactly the element type of useVehicles().data, eliminating type friction in the find/return paths.

L7-24 the precedence/sticky-picker JSDoc is preserved and restated in the file header: the four-tier order, the URL->store write-back 'sticky picker' intent, and the graceful 'does NOT throw if the store provider is missing' promise are all captured; the header documents that tiers 1 & 2 collapse out on native (no router) leaving store > first-vehicle.

L26-35 `export interface SelectedVehicleResult { vehicleId: number | null; vehicle: Vehicle | null; vehicles: Vehicle[]; setVehicleId: (id: number | null) => void }` preserved VERBATIM including all four field doc-comments (only the `vehicleId` doc tweaked from 'URL > store > first vehicle' to 'store > first vehicle' to match the native precedence).

L37-41 `parseId(raw)` preserved with byte-identical body (`if (raw == null || raw === '') return null; const n = Number(raw); return Number.isFinite(n) && n > 0 ? n : null;`). The only change is widening the parameter type from `string | null | undefined` to `string | number | null | undefined` so the same validator gates writes into the native store setter (web used it solely to parse URL string params, which are gone); Number(number) is identity so behavior is unchanged. Documented in the function JSDoc.

L43-44 `export function useSelectedVehicle(): SelectedVehicleResult` + `const { vehicleId: stored, setVehicleId } = useSelectedVehicleStore()` -> the function keeps its name/signature; `stored` is read from the inlined store via `useSyncExternalStore(subscribeSelection, getSelectionSnapshot, getSelectionSnapshot)` and `setVehicleId` aliases the stable module-level `setStoredVehicleId`. The store internals (`selectedVehicleId` let, `selectionListeners` Set, `setStoredVehicleId` with parseId validation + change-guard + listener fan-out, `subscribeSelection`, `getSelectionSnapshot`) are the VehicleSelect.tsx parity store, shared app-wide. L45 `const { data: vehicles } = useVehicles()` preserved verbatim (data typed Vehicle[] | undefined).

L47-51 path-param precedence (`useMatch('/vehicles/:id')`, `useMatch('/vehicles/:id/access')`, `parseId(...params.id)`) and L53-55 query-param precedence (`useSearchParams()`, `parseId(searchParams.get('vehicle_id'))`) are DROPPED — react-router-only. L57 `const urlId = pathId ?? queryId` is therefore permanently null on native; an inline comment documents this and that the precedence reduces to store > first vehicle.

L59-65 the URL->store write-back effect (`useEffect(() => { if (urlId != null && urlId !== stored) setVehicleId(urlId) }, [urlId, stored, setVehicleId])`) is NOT wired because `urlId` is always null on native (no router source can ever populate it); documented inline so the sticky-picker intent is preserved for future re-wiring without dead code.

L67-74 the default-to-first-vehicle block is preserved: `const firstVehicleId = vehicles && vehicles.length > 0 ? vehicles[0].id : null` is byte-identical, and the effect `if (stored == null && firstVehicleId != null) setVehicleId(firstVehicleId)` is preserved with deps `[stored, firstVehicleId]` (the stable module-level setter is intentionally not a dep, matching VehicleSelect.tsx and react-hooks/exhaustive-deps, which does not require module-scope functions).

L76-77 `const effectiveId = urlId ?? stored ?? firstVehicleId` -> `const effectiveId = stored ?? firstVehicleId` (the `urlId ??` tier is removed since urlId is always null); the inline-computation rationale ('so first-render reads don't wait for the effect') is preserved in the comment. L79-82 the `useMemo<Vehicle | null>` vehicle lookup (`if (effectiveId == null || !vehicles) return null; return vehicles.find(v => v.id === effectiveId) ?? null`) is preserved VERBATIM with the same `[effectiveId, vehicles]` deps.
L84-89 the return object `{ vehicleId: effectiveId, vehicle, vehicles: vehicles ?? [], setVehicleId }` is preserved VERBATIM. L90-91 closing brace + trailing newline preserved.

No DOM-only modules, browser HTML elements, Recharts, Leaflet, or web UI components imported — only react (useEffect / useMemo / useSyncExternalStore) and the ported useVehicles hook. Gates run from apps/native: npm run typecheck (tsc --noEmit); npm run lint -- --quiet; npm test -- --runInBand --detectOpenHandles.
